claims.text: Two screening tests: high-risk HPV testing and the Pap test (cervical cytology).
claims.quote: Two types of screening tests for cervical abnormalities are used: Testing for high-risk HPV genotypes Pap test (cervical cytology)

claims.text: ASCUS on a Pap alone: reflex HPV testing is the preferred follow-up.
claims.quote: For patients screened with a Pap test alone, if the cytology result is ASCUS (atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance), which is an inconclusive finding, HPV testing is the preferred method of follow-up evaluation; this approach is called reflex HPV testing.

claims.text: HPV negative: repeat screening in 3 years; if HPV positive, colposcopy.
claims.quote: If HPV testing is negative, screening tests should be repeated in 3 years. If HPV testing is positive, colposcopy should be done.

claims.text: Cervical bleeding or a visible lesion: cervical biopsy when the lesion or an abnormal Pap result calls for it.
claims.quote: Cervical biopsy is performed if the cervix is the source of the bleeding, and there is a cervical lesion or abnormal Papanicolaou (Pap) test result that indicates biopsy.

notes.issue: Doc paragraph carried a literal '**HPV positive:**' that the claim text lacked.
notes.resolution: Revised to 'HPV negative: repeat screening in 3 years; if HPV positive, colposcopy.' (lead-in bold only); re-checked OK by shay-49353 at 2026-10-05T02:36Z.
